claims.exact_statement: Let Phi be a finite-dimensional unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint channel and K=2Phi-I. If a trace-preserving EB channel Lambda satisfies the quadratic-form inequality Sym(Lambda) >= K on the Hermitian normalized-HS space, then Lambda is bistochastic and there is a canonical same-effect/same-preparation channel Gamma generated by one POVM with Gamma >= Sym(Lambda) >= K. Consequently feasibility among all EB channels is equivalent to feasibility among canonical POVM channels, with the same operator-order constant.
assumptions: Phi is unital, trace-preserving, and Hilbert-Schmidt self-adjoint
Lambda is trace-preserving and entanglement breaking
comparison is Loewner order or equivalently the stated quadratic-form comparison
claims.status: internally proved exact finite-dimensional reduction; not externally reviewed
claims.novelty_boundary: Finite Holevo form is standard prior art. The PSD majorization identity is a direct internal derivation. It does not prove the all-Q support inequality or factor-two theorem.
claims.costs: For an r-outcome Holevo representation the construction uses at most 2r canonical outcomes; finite Choi/Caratheodory form gives finite support but no efficient optimization or finite-precision construction is claimed.
claims.falsifier: An EB channel satisfying the assumed quadratic domination for which symmetrization is not bistochastic, or a failure of the exact identity (Gamma_M+Gamma_N)/2 - (Lambda+Lambda*)/2 = (1/2) sum_y |u_y-v_y><u_y-v_y|.
claims.next_gate: Prove the canonical support inequality for every positive Q and every legal self-compatible channel, or give a feasible broadcaster Choi state and global moment-dual violation.

claims.exact_statement: For arbitrary finite-dimensional unital, trace-preserving, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint self-compatible channels, it remains unresolved whether there exists one full-domain EB map Psi satisfying I-Psi <= 2(I-Phi), equivalently whether the canonical support inequality holds for every positive Hilbert-Schmidt dual Q.
assumptions: a full-domain two-output CPTP broadcaster with both marginals Phi is supplied
claims.status: UNKNOWN; no proof and no legal counterexample found in this cycle
claims.novelty_boundary: Existing almost-commuting results are for pairs or fixed-size tuples with size-dependent moduli; they do not supply the channel-energy-weighted common measurement for growing frames.
claims.costs: The theorem is an existence statement on supplied channels. Tree methods incur logarithmic rank; no dimension-free complexity claim is made.
claims.falsifier: A full proof of the all-Q support inequality, or a legal symmetric broadcaster Choi state and positive Q with a rigorous global moment-dual support deficit.
